input: This is synthetic workshop roleplay. I propose a scheduling tool for my 20-person dance club after personally missing a rehearsal. I can reach five members. Existing group chat has polls but two members said they missed a changed time; recurrence and switching remain unverified. I want chat, profiles, payments, badges, reminders, a calendar, and analytics. Narrow it and propose one concrete test now. Reply as raw JSON with features (a nonempty array of at most three feature names), participants (a nonempty string), action (a nonempty string), measure (a nonempty string), threshold (a nonempty string describing a proposed measurable criterion before testing), basis (a nonempty string labeling observations versus assumptions), result (use "not run"), demand_proven (boolean), questions (a string with 1-5 questions). Do not postpone the experiment behind background questions.
output: {"features":["Time-change alert sent directly to each member when a rehearsal time changes","Explicit acknowledgement reply captured for each alert"],"participants":"Proposal: the 5 dance club members the student says they can reach. Group size 20 (supplied); realistically contactable = 5 (supplied); actually contacted = Unknown.","action":"Run manually, no software. For the next 2 rehearsals where the time changes, the student posts the change in the existing group chat as usual AND separately sends each of the 5 reachable members a direct one-line message stating the new time and asking them to reply 'got it'. The student logs, per member per change: whether an acknowledgement came back, how long it took, and whether that member arrived at the correct new time. If no time change occurs within 2 rehearsal cycles, the student announces one deliberate practice change and runs the same procedure.","measure":"Per member per time change: (a) acknowledgement received within 12 hours yes/no, (b) arrival at the correct changed time yes/no. Also logged: how many time changes actually occurred in the window (recurrence, currently unverified).","threshold":"Set before testing: across the 5 members, at least 4 of 5 acknowledge within 12 hours, AND at least 4 of 5 arrive at the correct changed time, AND at least 1 real time change occurs within 2 rehearsal cycles. If any of the three fails, do not build the tool: if changes are rarer than 1 in 2 cycles, the missed-time problem may not recur enough to justify anything and the student should investigate frequency first; if acknowledgement is high but attendance still misses, the gap is not notification and the student should pivot to finding the real cause; if acknowledgement itself is low, test whether a different channel reaches people before assuming a new app would.","basis":"Synthetic workshop roleplay - not field evidence. Observed/supplied: student 'personally missing a rehearsal' (own experience); 'two members said they missed a changed time' (secondhand report, 2 people); group is 20 people; 5 reachable; 'existing group chat has polls'. Assumption (not established): that a direct, acknowledged alert would have prevented these misses - the supplied facts establish that misses happened around a changed time, not why the chat post did not land. Assumption: that the two members and the student would use a new channel at all. Unknown: recurrence rate of time changes, willingness to switch off the existing chat, what the two members actually did when they missed the change, whether anyone currently uses a workaround, whether any activity or payment cost exists. Deferred features and why: profiles, payments, badges, calendar, analytics, and in-app chat are all deferred because none of them is exercised by this test and none has a supplied observation behind it; the group already has a working chat with polls, so replacing it is unsupported.","result":"not run","demand_proven":false,"questions":"1. Over the last two months, how many rehearsal times actually changed? 2. What did each of the two members who missed a changed time do at the moment they realized - did they check anything, ask anyone, or nothing? 3. Do you approve running this manual 2-cycle test with the 5 members as written, or do you want to narrow, investigate recurrence first, or pivot?"}
